battle.name: 第三次布匿戰爭
battle.brief: 公元前149年，羅馬以迦太基違約攻擊努米底亞為由，渡海包圍北非迦太基城；前146年破城而入，巷戰數日，城市焚燒、居民販為奴隸。卡面的秦弩屬先秦中國兵器，地中海世界並無此制式：守城一方靠弓與石弩、配重投射器壓制攻城者，羅馬則以土壘進逼，兩者在守牆投射器上功能相對。

kit.name: 秦弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，射速遠勝拉弓。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 第三次布匿戰爭（公元前149年至前146年）是羅馬共和國與迦太基城邦之間的第三度全面衝突，全部戰事都發生在迦太基自己的土地上，即今北非突尼斯一帶，沒有一場會戰在羅馬本土或希臘發生。羅馬一方的決策層是元老院與人民大會，戰時最高統帥是兩名年度執政官：前149年渡海的是盧基烏斯·科爾內利烏斯·倫圖盧斯與普布利烏斯·科爾內利烏斯·西庇阿·納西卡，另有一套依晚期編年重建的說法把兩人記作馬尼利烏斯·馬尼利烏斯與盧基烏斯·馬爾基烏斯·凱爾索里努斯；開戰之後元老院另派十人委員會赴非洲監督善後。羅馬軍是公民兵與盟邦部隊的混合體，步兵按軍團、大隊、百人隊編制作戰，騎兵約四千人，最要緊的外部依賴是羅馬盟友努米底亞王國提供的騎兵；馬西尼撒的兩位王子轉投羅馬之後，迦太基多年來唯一能與羅馬騎兵抗衡的兵力便消失了。迦太基一方的體制是百人院與蘇菲特（suffete）組成的城市議會，公民兵、解放奴隸與各地雇傭兵組成軍團，另有不足一千人的「聖隊」以及象兵、戰車與常備騎兵作為骨幹，並有工匠團操持城防工事。第三方角色同樣清楚：烏提卡在開戰前倒向羅馬並提供港口與船塢，馬西尼撒諸子中有人出逃羅馬，希臘出身的傭兵將領希米爾科與狄奧根尼斯掌握實際作戰指揮，埃涅普等外省布匿城市有的堅持抵抗、有的開城投降。這是一場以公民軍對城邦國防的消耗戰，形態與第二次布匿戰爭那樣的野戰決戰完全不同。
countriesEn: The Third Punic War (149–146 BC) was the third and complete confrontation between the Roman Republic and the city-state of Carthage, and every episode of it took place in Carthaginian territory, in what is now northern Tunisia; not one pitched battle was fought in Italy or in Greece. On the Roman side, the decision belonged to the Senate and the assembly of the people, and the supreme command in the field was held by the two annual consuls: the pair that crossed the sea in 149 BC were Lucius Cornelius Lentulus and Publius Cornelius Scipio Nasica, while a reconstruction based on the late chronologies names Manius Manilius and Lucius Marcius Censorinus instead; after the declaration of war the Senate additionally sent a commission of ten men to Africa to supervise the settlement. The Roman army was a mixture of citizen troops and allied contingents, its infantry organised in legions, cohorts and centuries, with about four thousand cavalry, and its most important external dependence was the cavalry supplied by its ally, the kingdom of Numidia; once two of Masinissa's princes went over to Rome, the only force that could stand against Roman horse in the field for Carthage was gone. On the Carthaginian side the structure was a city council of a hundred members together with the suffetes, with a citizen militia, manumitted slaves and mercenaries from many regions forming the army, and less than a thousand men in the Sacred Band, together with elephants, chariots and standing cavalry as the hard core, and corps of engineers working the defences. The part played by third parties is equally clear: Utica threw itself to Rome before the war began and provided the harbour and the shipyard, some of Masinissa's sons fled to Rome, Greek mercenary commanders such as Himilco and Diogenes directed the actual fighting, and outlying Punic towns either held out in resistance or opened their gates. This was a war of attrition between a citizen army and a city-state's defences, a form altogether unlike the pitched-field battles of the Second Punic War.
people: 推動開戰的是羅馬元老院裡的「迦太基必須毀滅」一派，其代表是老加圖。這位公元前151年出任監察官的元老在前153年隨使團到訪迦太基，返國時帶回一把無花果枝，藉此說明這座城市的財力正在恢復、前次戰敗不過是暫時的；此後他在元老院發言，末尾總要加一句「我認為迦太基必須毀滅」。反對派以納西卡為首，理由是留一個足以嚇住平民的強敵，反而有助於維持羅馬內部的均衡，兩種意見在元老院裡拉鋒了數年，最終開戰派佔了上風。真正決定戰局走向的是西庇阿·艾米里安，這位養子是前201年打贏扎馬戰役的西庇阿·阿非利加努斯的曾孫：前149年他還只是軍中的護民官，在奈斐里營地的潰退中以三百騎反覆衝鋒、掩護步兵脫身，又整頓軍紀，因此在代表前148年以執政官身分前往非洲；前147年春季他三十六歲，按《維利亞法》本不得競選執政官，但公眾的呼聲之下元老院破例讓他當選，並把非洲全權交給他一人，他於是成為這場圍城戰真正的指揮者。迦太基方面的核心人物是行政總督（boetarch）哈斯德魯巴，他是前207年戰歿於梅陶魯斯河一役的那位哈斯德魯巴的曾孫，起初主張向羅馬求和，後來奪取城內主導權，改為死守；最後階段真正指揮防禦的是西西里出身的希臘傭兵將領希米爾科，冬季宿營地與外省野戰部隊則由狄奧根尼斯率領。哈斯德魯巴最終以羅馬人許諾保其性命與自由為條件投降，他的妻子站在城垛上對西庇阿道祝，轉而痛罵丈夫怯懦，帶著幾個兒子走進艾什蒙神廟自焚。史家方面，出身於羅馬的希臘人質波里比烏斯自前147年起隨軍在場，寫下《歷史》第六卷；阿庇安在二世紀末補寫《布匿戰爭史》第八卷，是「三百名人質」與最後通牒那一段記述的主要來源。
peopleEn: The man who drove the war was the faction of the Roman Senate that held that Carthage must be destroyed, and its spokesman was Cato the Elder. This senator, censor from 151 BC, travelled to Carthage with an embassy in 153 BC and came home carrying a branch of figs, to show that the wealth of the city had recovered and that the earlier defeat had been no more than temporary; from then on he closed every speech in the Senate with the words that he thought Carthage must be destroyed. The opposing faction was headed by Nasica, on the argument that a fearsome rival left in being would keep the Roman populace in check and preserve the balance inside the city; the two views fought each other in the Senate for several years before the hawks prevailed. The figure who actually decided the course of the war was Scipio Aemilianus, the adopted grandson of Scipio Africanus, who had won the battle of Zama in 201 BC: in 149 BC he was still only a tribune, and he distinguished himself in the confused retreat before Nepheris by leading three hundred cavalry through a series of limited, disciplined charges that covered the infantry's withdrawal, and by enforcing discipline in the ranks; he went to Africa as consul for 148 BC, and when the elections of 147 BC came round, at thirty-six or thirty-seven years of age he was by the Lex Villia too young to stand for the consulship, but under the pressure of public demand the Senate set aside the age requirements and elected him, giving him sole command in Africa. Thus he became the real director of the siege. On the Carthaginian side the central figure was the boetarch Hasdrubal, a great-grandson of the Hasdrubal who fell at the Metaurus in 207 BC; at first he favoured making terms with Rome, but he later seized control of the city's government and committed himself to resistance. The man who actually directed the defence in the last phase was Himilco, a Greek mercenary commander from Sicily, while the winter quarters and the field army in the hinterland were led by Diogenes. Hasdrubal finally surrendered on Scipio's promise of his life and freedom, and his wife, watching from a rampart, blessed Scipio, turned instead on her husband, and walked with several of her sons into the temple of Eshmoun to burn. On the side of the historians, Polybius, a Greek who had come to Rome as a hostage, was in the camp from 147 BC onwards and wrote the sixth book of his Histories; Appian, at the end of the second century AD, added the eighth book of the Punic Wars, and is the principal source for the three hundred hostages and the final ultimatum.
kits: 卡面這件秦弩是中國的兵器，年代定在公元前二百年前後，即秦王政前後：木製弩身，前端張弦，弦上架一支帶羽的矢，中段的弩機把拉弦的力量存住，射手用腳踏上弦（蹏張），再扣下機括放矢。這種機構的好處在於「存力」：張滿弦的弩可以在城頭懸持待放，不會像弓那樣因久拉而失力，也不要求射手有長期拉滿的臂力，因此可以成排懸在城垛後，等一聲令下同時齊發，射速與射後再張的時間都優於弓箭。在中國的戰史上，秦弩的典型用法正是守城：戰國末年趙國死守邯鄲抵禦秦軍，與前260年秦趙長平之戰中趙軍以弩手據城垣，都是弩機集中使用於防禦的實例；秦代的兵馬俑坑裡也出土過成批的銅弩機，說明這件兵器在西秦已是標準配備。但地中海世界從來沒有弩：公元前二世紀的義大利與北非，用的是弓（希臘語稱 toxon，羅馬人叫 arcus 與 sagitta）與更原始的擲石索（fundulus），以及希臘化時期傳入的配重式投射器（ballista、 cheiroballista 與較早的 catapultus）。迦太基在繳械時交出的清單裡，據阿庇安記載，僅石弩就有六萬具，同時繳出二十萬套盔甲與兩千座投射器，其後兩個月內又趕造八千面盾、一萬八千柄劍、三萬支矛與六萬具石弩，並在內港建成一百二十艘船的艦隊。羅馬方面的單兵裝備是重標槍（pilum）、短劍（gladius）與大曲面盾（scutum），攻城器械則有可移動的覆蓋廊道（vinea）、攻牆用的土壘（agger，也就是西庇阿用來封死港口的長堤）與專門建造的磚砌高台——一座與城牆等高的磚造射擊平台，讓四千名羅馬兵在極近距離向城頭射擊。迦太基的守城重裝包括象兵（約一百頭，徵自內陸象群）、前兩次戰爭中曾立功的戰車隊、以及仍保有作戰力的精銳步兵「聖隊」與外籍傭兵；城內水源靠蓄水池與收集雨水的渠道維持，這在長圍城中比任何攻城器械都要緊要。
kitsEn: The Chinese crossbow on the card is a Chinese weapon, dated to about 200 BC, that is, to the reign of the first emperor of the Qin: a wooden stock with the bowstring at the front, a bolt with fletching lying in the groove, and a trigger mechanism in the middle that stores the draw, the archer stepping into a stirrup to cock it and then releasing the catch. The virtue of the mechanism lies in the storing of force: a crossbow held at full draw can be kept hanging on a parapet without losing tension, does not sap the arm of a man who must hold it there, and therefore can be ranged in rows along a wall and loosed all at once on a signal, giving both a higher rate of fire and a shorter time to re-cock than a bow. In Chinese history the typical employment of the Qin crossbow was precisely in defence: the defence of Handan by Zhao against Qin at the end of the Warring States, and the massed crossbowmen of Zhao on the walls of Changping in 260 BC, are both instances of the mechanism being concentrated for the defence of a city; the bronze trigger mechanisms recovered from the terracotta pits in China show that the weapon was standard equipment under the Qin. The Mediterranean world had no crossbow at all: Italy and North Africa in the second century BC knew the bow (Greek toxon, Latin arcus and sagitta), the older throwing sling for stones (fundulus), and the Greek-style artillery that had spread in the Hellenistic age, the ballista, the cheiroballista and the earlier catapultus. In the inventory handed over when Carthage was disarmed, Appian records some sixty thousand stone-throwing engines, together with two hundred thousand sets of armour and two thousand artillery pieces; within two months the city produced another eight thousand shields, eighteen thousand swords, thirty thousand spears and sixty thousand stone slings, and fitted out a fleet of a hundred and twenty ships in the inner harbour. The Roman soldier's personal equipment was the heavy javelin (pilum), the short sword (gladius) and the large curved shield (scutum), and the siege equipment included the movable covered gallery (vinea), the earthen ramp or agger — the very mound with which Scipio closed the harbour — and a purpose-built brick tower, a platform raised to the height of the city wall from which four thousand Romans could shoot onto the ramparts at point-blank range. The heavy elements of the Carthaginian defence included war elephants (about a hundred, drawn up from the herds of the interior), the chariot corps that had won renown in the two earlier wars, the picked infantry of the Sacred Band, and foreign mercenaries; the city's water was held up by its cisterns and its channels for collecting rain, and in a long siege that mattered more than any siege engine whatever.
tactics: 羅馬的戰法從頭到尾是一套海陸雙線的攻城術。海上控制是前提：迦太基的戰艦在繳械時全數駛到烏提卡港燒毀，此後羅馬巡邏隊封鎖沿岸，使城內無法從海上取得補給；但以當時的航海技術，要真正切斷海上偷運極難，於是西庇阿另闢蹊徑，在港口一側築起一道長堤（mole），把港池與外海的通路逐步封死，迦太基的回應是從港內另挖一條通往大海的水道，並趕造新艦隊出奇襲擊，雙方在港內一戰各有勝負，撤退時迦太基的船卻被擠在城牆下，或沉或被俘。陸上，羅馬先後犯了兩次錯誤：前149年強攻城牆失敗，營地又選在瘴氣重的海灘，疫病肆行，營區被迫遷移而防禦力下降；執政官馬尼利烏斯不顧反對強攻迦太基野戰營，推進到無法退出的位置，遭迦太基反擊幾乎全軍覆沒，靠西庇阿的三百騎反覆掩護才撤回營地。前147年西庇阿接任後作風一變：先把主力營地移回迦太基城下近海，逼敵反應；再以嚴明軍紀整頓部隊，開除一批紀律鬆散者；接著夜襲入城，以四千人突入城內，雖然得手，卻因天亮後守軍可能重整而主動撤回，不貪一時之利。他的戰術核心是工程與射界：在港區建成與城牆等高的磚造平台，讓羅馬兵可以近距離射擊城頭；再以大軍分數路夜襲野戰營，攻下冬季宿營地，迫使外省城市逐一開城。前146年春天，總攻自港區方向發動，羅馬兵沿著長堤與磚台接近城牆，破口而入，接著以六天時間系統性地逐街推進，先肅清一條街再放火燒掉身後的房舍，把城牆變成推進的堡壘；被逼到艾什蒙神廟的九百名羅馬逃兵死守到底，與神廟同焚。迦太基的防禦是典型的深層堡壘：外圍有壕溝，中間是厚九米、高十五至二十米的磚牆，最內是古老的舊牆；城內靠蓄水池與雨水渠維持水源，餓死守軍的時間與糧食的存耗同樣重要。迦太基的出擊則以奇襲與騷擾為主：派出八千人的支隊盯住羅馬營地、以火船襲擊停泊的羅馬艦船、夜間襲擾糧道，並在羅馬攻勢的間隙裡以象兵與「聖隊」反覆出擊。
tacticsEn: The Roman method was, from beginning to end, a siege technique operating by land and sea at once. Control of the sea was the precondition: Carthage's warships were all sailed round to the harbour of Utica and burnt, and from then on Roman patrols closed the coast so that the city could draw no supplies from the sea; but with the navigation of the age it was very hard to stop the blockade runners outright, and Scipio found another way, raising a great mole on the harbour side and gradually sealing the passage between the inner basin and the open sea. Carthage answered by cutting a new channel from the harbour to the sea and by building a fresh fleet for a surprise sortie; the engagement in the harbour was indecisive, but when the Carthaginians withdrew at the end of the day many of their ships were trapped against the city wall and either sunk or captured. On land the Romans made two mistakes. In 149 BC they assaulted the walls without success, and one of the two camps was so badly sited on the beach that it became pestilential by early summer and had to be moved to healthier ground at the cost of its defensibility; and the consul Manilius, against advice, attacked the main Carthaginian field camp, advanced into a position he could not hold, and was counter-attacked so heavily that only Scipio's three hundred cavalry, charging in disciplined bounds, kept the army from being destroyed. When Scipio took over in 147 BC his whole approach changed. He moved the main camp back to the sea below the city to force a reaction; he enforced discipline and dismissed a number of men he judged slack or unwilling; he then made a night attack into the town with four thousand men and, having gained the city by surprise, withdrew of his own accord rather than risk being reorganised against him in daylight. The core of his method was engineering and field of fire: he raised the brick platform in the harbour quarter to the height of the wall so that his men could shoot at the ramparts from close range; he then struck the field army's winter camp from several directions at night, overran it, and forced the outlying towns to open their gates one after another. In the spring of 146 BC the general assault came from the harbour quarter, the Romans working along the mole and the brick platform until they forced a breach; then they spent six days pushing systematically street by street, clearing a quarter before firing the houses behind them, so that the wall itself became the platform of the advance; and the nine hundred Roman deserters who were driven back to the temple of Eshmoun held out to the end and burned the temple with themselves. The Carthaginian defence was that of a fortified depth: a ditch outside, in the middle a brick wall nine metres thick and fifteen to twenty metres high, and at the innermost the ancient old wall; inside the city, cisterns and rainwater channels kept the water going, and the length of time it would take to starve the defenders mattered as much as the stores of grain. The Carthaginian counterstroke was by surprise and harassment: a detachment of eight thousand shadowed the Roman camp, fireships were sent against the Roman ships beached in the lagoon, the supply lines were raided by night, and between the Roman attacks the elephants and the Sacred Band sallied out again and again.
data: 有根據可寫的數字大致如下。羅馬投入的兵力，阿庇安記為八萬四千兵，現代史家多估為四萬至五萬人，其中騎兵約四千人；元老院另派十人委員會。迦太基方面的野戰軍隊至少兩萬人，前147年冬營被破時由狄奧根尼斯率領；前147年冬天負責監視羅馬營地者為八千人；前147年那次夜襲入城，羅馬投入四千人；前149年戰局中有一名努米底亞首領率二千二百人轉投羅馬。繳械清單數目最大：二十萬套盔甲、兩千座投射器；其後兩個月趕造八千面盾、一萬八千柄劍、三萬支矛、六萬具石弩，另建一百二十艘船。城防數字：城牆周長三十五公里以上，護城壕寬二十米，主磚牆厚九米、高十五至二十米，牆內營房可容二萬四千兵；城市人口估算從九萬到八十萬不等，眾說紛紜。圍城歷時約三年，最終總攻自前146年春天開始，史料對城破後的焚燒日數說法不一：波里比烏斯記為十七日，阿庇安記為三日，今日通行敘述多採六日的系統性巷戰。城破之日，除九百名死守神廟的羅馬逃兵外，約五萬名迦太基人投降並被販為奴隸。戰前舊事亦可對照：前201年和約規定迦太基分五十年賠付一萬塔蘭特銀，並禁止未經羅馬同意在海外用兵；前151年賠款付清，與此同時迦太基卻出兵攻擊努米底亞而敗於奧羅斯科帕一役。戰後羅馬宣布迦太基土地為公地（ager publicus），一百二十二年的改革派一度試圖在舊址建「新殖民地」（Junonia）而被擱置，前一一一年再立法禁止，前二十九年奧古斯都才把重建完成。流傳的「羅馬人撒鹽於地」說法，基本可以確定是十九世紀以後才出現的。
dataEn: The figures that can be given on good authority are roughly these. The Roman force, Appian gives as 84,000 men, while modern historians generally estimate 40,000 to 50,000, of whom about four thousand were cavalry; the Senate also sent a commission of ten. On the Carthaginian side the field army numbered at least 20,000, and was led by Diogenes in the winter of 147 BC, when its camp was overrun; a detachment of eight thousand shadowed the Roman camp in the winter of that year, and four thousand Romans were committed to the night attack into the city in 147 BC; and during the campaign of 149 BC one Numidian chief went over to Rome with 2,200 men. The largest set of numbers belongs to the disarmament: two hundred thousand sets of armour and two thousand artillery pieces; and within the following two months the city turned out eight thousand shields, eighteen thousand swords, thirty thousand spears and sixty thousand stone slings, while fitting out a fleet of a hundred and twenty ships. As for the defences: the circuit of the walls exceeded 35 kilometres, the ditch in front was 20 metres wide, the principal brick wall was 9 metres thick and 15 to 20 metres high, and the barracks inside it could hold over 24,000 men; estimates of the city's population range from 90,000 to 800,000, and no one can fix it. The siege lasted about three years, and the final assault opened in the spring of 146 BC; the ancient sources differ on the length of the burning that followed the city's fall, Polybius giving seventeen days, Appian three, while the narrative generally used today follows the six days of systematic street fighting. On the day the city fell, apart from nine hundred Roman deserters who died holding the temple, some 50,000 Carthaginians surrendered and were sold into slavery. Older context can be set beside these: the peace of 201 BC required Carthage to pay ten thousand silver talents over fifty years and forbade it to wage war without Roman permission; the indemnity was paid off in 151 BC, and in that same year Carthage attacked Numidia in breach of the treaty and was defeated at Oroscopa. After the war Rome declared the land of Carthage to be public land (ager publicus); in 122 BC the reformist faction tried to establish a new settlement on the site, the Junonia, and the plan was dropped; in 111 BC the prohibition was renewed by statute, and only in 29 BC did Augustus carry the rebuilding through. The familiar story of the Romans sowing the ruins with salt can now be treated as an invention of the nineteenth century or later.
cause: 直接起因是迦太基在和約限制下的一次違規用兵。公元前201年扎馬戰役後的和約剝奪了迦太基的海外領地，並禁止它在未經羅馬明示許可時對海外用兵；羅馬的盟友努米底亞王馬西尼撒便藉此不斷侵奪迦太基在利比亞的城池，前151年甚至奪走大萊普提斯等城，迦太基向羅馬申訴，元老院的調解卻總是偏袒馬西尼撒。前151年，迦太基在沒有羅馬許可的情況下出兵反攻努米底亞，主將哈斯德魯巴在奧羅斯科帕一役大敗，軍隊投降，本人逃回城中被判死刑；這次違約立刻被羅馬的反迦太基派抓住，成為開戰的現成藉口。此時羅馬國內的推力也齊備：老加圖從前153年起就以無花果枝為象徵鼓吹毀滅迦太基，擔心迦太基商業競爭、擔心馬西尼撒一旦去世而秩序失控、以及想把迦太基當作轉移國內矛盾的對象，各種動機交疊。公元前150年，羅馬派出使團仲裁馬西尼撒諸子馬西尼薩與馬西瓦之間的繼承糾紛，迦太基拒絕交出這兩位王子，使團隨即要求迦太基繳械；繳械完成後，執政官又提出撤出城外十英里、由羅馬拆毀城市的最後通牒，迦太基在悲憤中殺死城內所有羅馬人、驕逐使團，議會正式宣戰。前149年，烏提卡倒向羅馬並交出港口，羅馬元老院與人民大會隨即宣戰，大軍在烏提卡登陸。
causeEn: The immediate cause was an illicit use of force by Carthage under the restrictions of the peace treaty. After the battle of Zama in 201 BC the treaty stripped Carthage of its overseas territories and forbade it to wage war without the express permission of Rome; Rome's ally, Masinissa, king of Numidia, exploited this repeatedly, seizing the towns of Carthage's Libyan province and, by 151 BC, taking Lepteis Magna and other cities, and when Carthage appealed to Rome the Senate's arbitration consistently favoured Masinissa. In 151 BC Carthage struck back against Numidia without Roman permission, and its commander Hasdrubal was beaten at Oroscopa and surrendered with his army; he escaped back to the city and was there condemned to death, and this breach of the treaty was seized upon at once by the anti-Carthaginian faction in Rome as a ready-made pretext for war. The pushing forces inside Rome were now all in place: Cato had been beating the drum for the destruction of Carthage with his branch of figs since 153 BC; there was a fear of Carthaginian commercial competition, a fear of disorder on the death of the ageing Masinissa, and a wish to use Carthage as a target for the domestic quarrels of the city, and the motives overlapped. In 150 BC Rome sent a commission to arbitrate the succession dispute between Masinissa's sons Massinissa and Massiva, and Carthage refused to hand the two princes over; the commission then demanded the surrender of all the city's weapons, and when that had been done the consuls added the final ultimatum, that the population should move ten miles away from the sea and that the city itself should be destroyed. The Carthaginians, in a paroxysm, killed every Roman inside the walls and drove out the envoys, and the council formally declared war. In 149 BC Utica went over to Rome and handed over its harbour, and the Roman Senate and assembly declared war, the great army landing at Utica.
impact: 迦太基的毀滅是地中海世界政治版圖的分水嶺。此後再沒有任何一個國家能與羅馬在西地中海抗衡，羅馬也第一次真正接手海上霸權：從迦太基沒收的船隻與港口讓羅馬的艦隊不再只是臨時召集的水上民兵，而迦太基的耕地、埃及的穀物與北非的剩餘物產則被納入羅馬的糧食體系，阿非利加行省成為帝國最重要的穀倉之一，這正是羅馬後來在義大利本身歉收時真正的依仗。城市被拆毀之後，本地的布匿文化並未被連根拔除：羅馬沒有干涉私人的語言、信仰與習俗，頒給那些仍站到最後的城市一定的自治，龐特的語言在北非一直說到公元七世紀，被稱為「新布匿文明」；羅馬從迦太基掠獲的西西里神像與祭祀器物，後來被隆重送還原屬的城邦。政治上，「迦太基必須毀滅」成為羅馬政壇上一個可以反覆調用的口號：前121年，改革派蓋烏斯·格拉古想在新得到的公地上建「朱諾尼亞」殖民地而失敗；前一一一年元老院再立法禁止；一直到前二世紀末，凱撒才計畫在舊址重建羅馬城，前二十九年奧古斯都完成這件事，迦太基遂成為羅馬帝國在非洲的主要都會之一。另一面的代價也在數字之內：羅馬為此投入的軍費、消耗的兵員與在非洲拉長的補給線，換來的是一個不再有競爭者的地中海；而羅馬此後數百年間的政策，多數是在解決自己製造出來的這個空間——沒有宿敵的帝國，比有宿敵的共和國更難駕馭。
impactEn: The destruction of Carthage was the watershed of the political geography of the Mediterranean. After it no state could any longer compete with Rome in the western Mediterranean, and Rome for the first time genuinely assumed mastery of the sea: the ships and harbours taken from Carthage ended the condition in which the Roman fleet was merely an ad hoc levy of seamen, while the lands of Carthage, the grain of Egypt and the remaining produce of North Africa were drawn into the Roman food supply, and the province of Africa became one of the empire's chief granaries, the real stay of Rome in years when Italy itself failed. After the razing of the city the local Punic culture was not extirpated: Rome did not interfere with private language, religion or custom, granted a measure of self-government to the cities that had held out to the last, and the Punic language continued to be spoken in North Africa until the seventh century AD, in what is known as Neo-Punic civilisation; and the cult statues and sacred vessels that Carthage had plundered from the Sicilian cities were returned to their proper homes with great ceremony. Politically, the destruction of Carthage became a formula the Roman Forum could summon again and again: in 121 BC the reformer Gaius Gracchus tried to found the colony of Junonia on the new public land and failed; the Senate forbade resettlement again in 111 BC; only in the last years of the second century did Caesar plan to rebuild the site as a Roman city, and in 29 BC Augustus carried the work through, so that Carthage became one of the principal cities of the Roman Empire in Africa. The cost on the other side is contained in the numbers: the money, the men and the lengthened lines of supply that Rome spent in Africa bought a Mediterranean with no rival in it; and for the centuries that followed, the policy of the Roman state was largely occupied with managing the space it had made for itself, for an empire without an enemy proved harder to steer than a republic with one.
result: 前146年春天，港區方向被突破，羅馬軍以六天時間逐街肅清全城。哈斯德魯巴在得到西庇阿保其性命與自由的許諾後出城投降，他的妻子卻在城頭祝福羅馬將領、痛斥丈夫，並帶著兒子走進艾什蒙神廟投火而死；九百名在迦太基效力的羅馬逃兵退入同一座神廟，死守到最後，與神廟一同燒毀。約五萬名迦太基人被販為奴隸，城市被劫掠一空並被有意拆毀：元老院命西庇阿主持進一步的破壞，把迦太基土地宣布為公地，禁止任何人重新定居，並在城址上留下詛咒。羅馬軍回師，舉行凱旋式，西庇阿沿用其養祖父的名字，稱為「阿非利加努斯」。迦太基國家至此不復存在，也沒有任何和約：與迦太基站在最後的布匿城市被沒收為公地或被拆毀，仍能維持的城市則保留部分舊有制度；曾經站在羅馬一邊的烏提卡獲得自由，成為阿非利加行省的首府，北非的穀物從此經由迦太基海港這個舊樞紐運往羅馬。一百二十二年後，凱撒計畫在廢墟上重建這座城市，迦太基的廢墟至今仍留在今突尼斯市東南方約十公里處的海岸上。
resultEn: In the spring of 146 BC the harbour quarter was breached and the Romans cleared the city street by street over six days. Hasdrubal came out and surrendered on Scipio's promise of his life and freedom, while his wife on the rampart blessed the Roman general, denounced her husband for his cowardice, and walked into the temple of Eshmoun with her children to burn; the nine hundred Roman deserters in Carthaginian service were driven back into the same temple and held it to the end, burning with it. Some 50,000 Carthaginians were sold into slavery, and the city was plundered and deliberately levelled: the Senate ordered Scipio to carry out further demolitions, declared the land of Carthage to be public land, forbade anyone from resettling the site, and laid a curse upon it. The army returned to Rome, celebrated a triumph, and Scipio took the name of his adoptive grandfather, Africanus. The state of Carthage ceased to exist, and there was no treaty: the Punic towns that had stood by Carthage to the end were confiscated as public land or destroyed, those that survived were allowed to keep some part of their old institutions; and Utica, which had sided with Rome, was left free and made the capital of the province of Africa, through which the grain of North Africa now flowed to Rome by way of the old port of Carthage. A century and a half later Caesar planned to rebuild the city on the ruins, and the ruins of Carthage still lie on the coast about ten kilometres east of the modern city of Tunis.
